title: Duchy of Saint Sava
capsule: The Duchy of Saint Sava was founded by Stjepan Vukčić Kosača, who adopted the title Herceg (Herzog) of Saint Sava in autumn 1448 — invoking the miracle-working relics of the first Serbian Archbishop, enshrined at Mileševa monastery within his domains — a title whose regional resonance survives in the name Herzegovina. The duchy encompassed territories across modern Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Montenegro, positioning Kosača as effectively independent of the Bosnian crown. After Stjepan's death in 1466, his son Vlatko Hercegović held the shrinking coastal enclave around Novi against Ottoman pressure; Ottoman forces besieged Novi in autumn 1481, and it fell in late December 1481/January 1482, with the territory incorporated into the Ottoman Sanjak of Herzegovina.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's general extent is known from Ottoman cadastral records and Venetian and Ragusan reports, but mountainous interior boundaries were fluid and the dataset from=1453 likely reflects Kosača's reorganization after the fall of Bosnia.
